newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Second Malaysia national airline to fly on Nov 17.
newsitem.headline: Second Malaysia national airline to fly on Nov 17.

text.p: Malaysia's second national airline, Pacific Eagle, will begin scheduled flights on November 17, AirAsia Sdn Bhd director Tik Mustaffa was quoted as saying in the Business Times on Monday.
He told the daily the airline would begin with scheduled chartered flights to three regional destinations, Thailand, the Philippines and Taiwan. It plans to go global in five years.
The airline is operated by AirAsia, 85 percent owned by Hicom Holdings Bhd and 15 percent by Mofaz Air Sdn Bhd.
The airline's main focus would be the tourist market, he said. "If you look at the increase in passenger traffic, it is quite high and we are taking the opportunity to fulfil demand," Tik said.

AirAsia has authorised capital of 50 million ringgit and paid-up capital of 22 million. Initial investment will be around 700 million ringgit which covers operations costs, networking capital and the lease of two Boeing 737-300s for two years, Tik said.
At present Malaysia's sole national carrier is Malaysian Airline System Bhd.
The country has a number of other small airline companies which provide local and regional services, but only Pacific Eagle has been officially designated as the second national carrier.
